title: qt submodule needs updating
body:
I know that according to https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/5160 this project is no longer maintained however this is an effortless fix.

Currently the qt submodule is on commit [cb88757](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/qt/tree/cb88757e7c9383a0504689c8373c101a44214132) which doesn't include subsequent commits that fixed issues with gcc 9+.

So when you do:

`git clone --recursive https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf.git`

you get a version that doesn't compile with gcc 9+, until you do:

`git submodule update --recursive --remote`

I discovered this using wkhtmltopdf/packaging to build a package for Fedora 37 which I eventually managed to do for aarch64 and x86_64. I will open a PR with my work in due course.

title: Add the Possibility of Page Grouping
body:
**Description**
How can we add the possibility of creating a PDF with 15 pages, say, with all the pages numbered from 1 to 5?

So, we have a single PDF file that is generated with 15 pages, but the pages are numbered based on particular criteria (the value of a variable). This is particularly useful when you have to do this for pdf files that have many pages. If it's just a tiny file then we can always create them separately and join them somehow.

**Example**  
For example, we have a list of footballers in the USA from 3 states Ohio, Texas, and Florida. We've listed these footballers in order of their states. We want all the pages carrying Ohio players to be numbered from 1 to *, those for Texas 1 to *, etc, but all the 3 lists should be generated as one PDF. The variable here is the state! 

So if each state has players which can fill up 5 pages, then we'll have a 15-page pdf number 1-5 for Ohio, 1-5 for Texas, and 1-5 for Florida.

I would be happy to explain any doubts and look at any questions 😎

body:

This can be accomplished using Chromium version 13_0_767_1 which uses a very close version of WebKit.

I have created a [Gist](https://gist.github.com/JavaScriptDude/2a599a9ea3af1ff9477b4285d8051cfb) that explains how to do this for those who want to know.

title: Copy-pasting code from the PDF loses formatting
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6 (with patched qt)

**OS information**
Tested on MacOS Big Sur and Linux Mint Uma 20.2

**Description**
Code samples (for example, YAML or Python) are properly formatted in the pdf, but most of the formatting is lost when copy-pasting the code from the PDF into a text editor or terminal. Depending on the PDF viewer, either:
- line breaks are retained, but indentation is lost (evince, preview, adobe reader), or
- line breaks are lost and everything becomes a single line, but whitespace is retained (built-in pdf viewer of Firefox and VS Code)

See [test.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/7675214/test.pdf) for an example.

**How to reproduce**
1. Download and unzip [test.html.zip](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/7675212/test.html.zip)
2. Run `cat test.html | wkhtmltopdf - test.pdf`
3. Copy-paste the code from the PDF into a text editor

**Expected behavior**
The pasted code should have the same formatting as in the PDF, with proper indentation and linebreaks.

Removing the span and code tags from the HTML does not solve the problem.
Any help or workaround is greatly appreciated.

```
Loading pages (1/6)
Error: Failed loading page file:///C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/php3FC5.tmp (sometimes it will work just to ignore this error with --load-error-handling ignore)
Exit with code 1, due to unknown error.
```

**How to reproduce**

1. Run `.\wkhtmltopdf.exe php3FC5.tmp output.pdf`
2. Observe that it fails.
3. Rename input file from `php3FC5.tmp` to `php3FC5.html`.
4. Run `.\wkhtmltopdf.exe php3FC5.html output.pdf`
5. Observe that it works successfully.

**Expected behavior**
The program must work even the file extension is different than `.html`. If it is not possible, it must return a helpful error.

title: Auto documentation is very incomplete and vague - non-usable by "non-coders"
body:
**Description**  
<!-- A clear and concise description of the problem/improvement. -->
The only "documentation" for wkhtmltopdf is offered by the **man page** or, as stated elsewhere, the autodoc which is offered by 

`**wkhtmltopdf -H**`

It is NOT possible to use wkhtmltopdf properly with **ONLY** that information, which is the same content as the man page for it.

That help page should be **enough to fully master the tool** and allow new users to fully benefit from the tool's full capabilities, by being a self-contained whole which, **at this time, it is not**.

I sincerely thank all coders for their contributions to date in delivering what is widely touted as very reliable and useful tool.  I only wish, for an end-user as myself, that it was more usable.

EVERY command line option, for which a value must be assigned, should have the full set of legal values fully listed, along with explicit description of what such settings will trigger as an outcome.

Also, some options are mutually exclusive or conflicting.  These should be grouped to make such inter-dependencies or conflicts obvious to potential users.


**As it is, it is not possible to fully master wkhtmltopdf's stated high quality results without delving into its source code.**

Desktop users are not "coders".  They want to use tools that are offered with minimal effort, and most especially want to avoid the agony of trying to learn a foreign language (the application's source code) in order to make full use of the tool's capabilities.

I plead with all contributors to wkhtmltopdf's code to please consider this usability perspective and help attract new users to the Linux Desktop world by **making the "basic" documentation more self-contained** for full mastery of the tool. 

Thank you for hearing me out.

[DEMO__wkhtmltopdf__TestCase.zip  (revised)](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/7402193/DEMO__wkhtmltopdf__TestCase.zip)

[README_v2.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/7402229/README_v2.txt)

The "Unknown long argument" seems completely out-of-place, given that I used the man page's option line as the starting point (tweaked the literal) !!!

Format used for option is as literally used in the man pages, by substituting "footer" for "header", and substitution of "bottom" for "top" in the line taken from the man page:

```

              Add a default header, with the name of the page to the left, 
              and the page number to the right, this is short for:
              --header-left='[webpage]'   --header-right='[page]/[toPage]'   --top 2cm   --header-line
```
The substitutions which I made seem perfectly legitimate and logical, since the "header" and "footer" options should be "symmetrical" so to speak.  If "--top" is quoted and referenced, then so must a "--bottom" exist.

I also tried the format  "--header-right '[page]/[toPage]'"  with no success.  

For me ... that means something is broken.

On a lark, I even tried the header options instead of the footer options, using

`--header-center='[page]/[toPage]' --top 2cm --header-line`

body:
**Description**
<!-- A clear and concise description of the new feature. -->
Provide **specific reporting** of URL to identify any object which wkhtmltopdf is unable to locate.

**Example**  
<!-- A simple example of the new feature in action. -->
Note that I only recently started using wkhtmltopdf.

**I wasted a few hours** trying to figure out the nature of the "Error" message that provided below.  The totality of messaging with "--log-level info" is the following:

> Loading pages (1/6)
> Warning: Blocked access to file                                   
> Error: Failed to load about:blank, with network status code 301 and http status code 0 - Protocol "about" is unknown
> Counting pages (2/6)                                               
> Resolving links (4/6)                                                       
> Loading headers and footers (5/6)                                           
> Printing pages (6/6)
> Done                                                                          
> Exit with code 1 due to network error: ProtocolUnknownError

It turns out that this was because there were missing graphics image files (or more correctly stated, graphics files with the wrong names) !!!

This frustration during ramp-up in usage of wkhtmltopdf could have been avoided, and made the experience much more encouraging, **if wkhtmltopdf had provided a report of the full URL specification for the image or content that the tool was unable to locate** while building the final output.

Could you please incorporate this more user-friendly approach to messaging?

``` Example wkhtmltopdf output ``` Loading pages (1/6) =============================> ] 50% ``` Running `strace` on the wkhtmltopdf process seemingly shows `mmap` calls in an infinite loop (below output repeats indefinitely): ``` mmap(NULL, 32768, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0cef38000 mmap(NULL, 32768, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0cef30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0cee30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0ced30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0cec30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0ceb30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0cea30000 mmap(NULL, 1048576, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) = 0x7fa0ce930000 ``` The process is eventually killed by the OOM killer. Doing any one of these fixes the problem: * Remove style for `code` in the header. * Remove style for `body` in the header. * Remove inline `margin-left` style for code, or set the value to `0`. * Remove the space in front of the `-Identity` text. * Add a line break after the opening `code` tag and before the `-Identity` text. * Add add any other text between the opening `code` tag and the space before the `-Identity` text. * Changing `pre` to another tag. For clarity: * It does not matter what the `-Identity` text is, only that there is a space after the opening `code` tag and before some text begins. * The `code` tag can be changed to another inline tag and the same problem will occur (tag in header style must be changed also). **How to reproduce** Using the above HTML, attempt to generate a PDF using basic options: ``` wkhtmltopdf --encoding UTF-8 file:////PATH/TO/HTML_FILE /PATH/TO/OUTPUT_FILE ``` **Expected behavior** The PDF should generate successfully.

body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.6 **OS information** Windows 10 (latest) **Description** When rendering content that contains `
` tags the rendered content often breaks in the middle of a line with half the line rendering in upper page, and the other half in the lower:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1374013/128619504-dfa77aba-4fdb-45d4-a4b1-75417edf774b.png)


The specific use case for me is that I have code blocks in a rendered markdown document that render something like this:

```html

     package cse41321.algorithms;

import java.util.NoSuchElementException;

public class Homework6 {
  /**
   * A generic BinaryTree class
   *
   * @param
   */

...



```

Although this has `` tags inside of it, also tried with plain text content (ie. just code) and it behaves the same.

The same code renders fine in Chromium Print Preview and PDF generation. The same code also doesn't show the syntax coloring that is applied via JavaScript, while that **does show** in Chromium print preview and in generated PDF through  Print.


[PDF_With_Code_Pagebreak_Bug.zip](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6950168/PDF_With_Code_Pagebreak_Bug.zip)

**How to reproduce**

I've attached the saved HTML file with dependencies to duplicate. 

generated with:

```ps
"wkhtmltopdf.exe" --enable-local-file-access --image-dpi 300 --page-size Letter --orientation Portrait --enable-internal-links --keep-relative-links --print-media-type --encoding utf-8 --footer-font-size 0 "C:\Temp\README.html" "C:\Temp\README.pdf" 
```

**Expected behavior**

Page breaks should not split lines of code but break on line boundaries. This appears to work fine for non-`
` text, but doesn't with `
` text.

Also tested this with **just plain `
` text (with out `` and without the JS coloring applied and it still breaks incorrectly.

title: All logs written by progressfeedback.cc are written to stderr
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.6

**Description**
All logs written by progressfeedback.cc are written to stderr, including even helper functions that are supposed to be for writing info or warning level.
For example:
```
void ProgressFeedback::info(const QString &message) {
	if (logLevel < settings::Info) return;
	fprintf(stderr, "Info: %s",S(message));
	finishLine(6 + message.size());
}
```
as you can see this info log is being written to `stderr`.

**How to reproduce**
Simply convert an image and monitor the output streams.
`wkhtmltoimage yourfile.html yourfile.png`

**Expected behavior**
I would expect that logs would be written to the appropriate output stream. For example info->stdout, error->stderr. This is causing issues for us in application monitoring be cause simple info level logs are being reported as errors.

**Possible Solution**  
Update logging and progress feedback functions to write to `stdout` or `stderr` as necessary

title: wkhtmltopdf converts PNG images to JPEG
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.6 (no patched qt) **OS information** NixOS 20.03 **Description** When using `wkhtmltopdf` on a simple HTML file (containing a mix of text and PNG images), the PNGs get embedded in the PDF as JPEGs, resulting in a dramatic increase in file size. I know the PNGs are PDF-embeddable in the first place because I got them out of another PDF with `pdfimages -all`! **How to reproduce** Get some PNGs. Here I unpack them from an existing PDF I have, but I've also tried it with random PNGs downloaded from the internet, PNG screenshots, etc, and gotten the same results, so you can use whatever you have handy. ``` $ pdfimages -f 8 -l 8 -all input.pdf page-007; identify page-007-* page-007-000.png PNG 1998x750 1998x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 57490B 0.000u 0:00.000 page-007-001.png PNG 1957x750 1957x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 64361B 0.000u 0:00.000 page-007-002.png PNG 1992x750 1992x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 84161B 0.000u 0:00.000 ``` A simple HTML file embedding them. I've stripped out all the textual content, CSS, and whatnot to make this as minimal as possible. ``` $ cat test.html


``` Turn it into a PDF, then peel the images back out with `pdfimages` and take a look... ``` $ wkhtmltopdf --enable-local-file-access --quiet \ -B 0 -T 0 -L 0 -R 0 \ --page-width 24cm --page-height 100cm \ test.html test.pdf $ pdfimages -all test.pdf test; identify test-* test-000.jpg JPEG 1998x750 1998x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 459263B 0.000u 0:00.000 test-001.jpg JPEG 1957x750 1957x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 517676B 0.000u 0:00.000 test-002.jpg JPEG 1992x750 1992x750+0+0 8-bit sRGB 628325B 0.000u 0:00.000 ``` And see that all the images have turned into much larger JPEGs, which explains the file size of the resulting PDF as well: ``` $ du -shc --apparent-size page-007-* 202K total $ du -sh --apparent-size test.pdf 1.3M test.pdf ``` This also causes me to wonder if JPEG files in the input are getting recompressed; if I roundtrip them through `wkhtmltopdf`+`pdfimages` the file sizes change, although of course the difference isn't nearly as dramatic as for PNG->JPEG. **Expected behavior** The PNG files are embedded as-is, keeping their original quality and file size.

title: [Feature Request] Allow for direct footer and header html
Images not reused when other images get loaded
body: Hi! We noticed some strange behavior with wkhtmltopdf. When reusing the same images, wkhtmltopdf doesn't reuse the images and adds them for a second time to the pdf. This largely increases the pdf size. ------------------ ### Example #1 - Two different images ``` ``` **Output: 5.2 MB** ------------------ ### Example #2 - Two different images, last image gets repeated ``` ``` **Output: 5.2 MB** (same as the two images example) ------------------ ### Example #3 - Two different images, each image after each other ``` ``` **Output: 7.9 MB** (this increases the pdf size.. but the images are the same) ------------------ How is this possible? Does wkhtmltopdf not reuse the image when they are the same? I've tested this also with local files, same issue. The problem occurs when the previous image repeat gets stopped by a new image. But the image that then gets loaded is still the same as the other already loaded/added images.

title: Incorrect layout when explicitly setting PDF page size for standalone SVG in wkhtmltopdf 0.13
body: **wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.13 Installed from MSYS2 on Windows 10 ``` $ wkhtmltopdf.exe --version wkhtmltopdf 0.13 ``` **OS information** Windows 10, using MSYS2 ``` $ systeminfo.exe ... OS Name: Microsoft Windows 10 Home OS Version: 10.0.19042 N/A Build 19042 OS Manufacturer: Microsoft Corporation OS Configuration: Standalone Workstation OS Build Type: Multiprocessor Free ... ``` **Description** When converting standalone `.svg` files, the PDF output seems if the page size is explicitly set to the size of the SVG file. (the same happens if I wrap the SVG in an "empty" HTML file, like this: ```html ``` ) **How to reproduce** First, I made a test SVG in Inkscape 1.0.2, with explicit size of 1000 x 200 pts (*just rename from `\*.svg.txt` to `\*.txt`; Github doesn't allow .svg attachments*) * [test_inkscape.svg.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6364857/test_inkscape.svg.txt) Here is the PDF that Inkscape itself produces: * [test_inkscape.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6364862/test_inkscape.pdf) ``` $ pdfinfo test_inkscape.pdf | grep 'Page size' Page size: 1000 x 200 pts ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48317456/115864161-cc6fcb80-a436-11eb-97a1-8fc716216cac.png) ----- Here is the PDF produced by `wkhtmltopdf` without extra arguments - it exports PDF on A4 paper by default: ``` $ wkhtmltopdf.exe test_inkscape.svg test_inkscape_wk0.pdf Loading page (1/2) Printing pages (2/2) Done ``` * [test_inkscape_wk0.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6364891/test_inkscape_wk0.pdf) ``` $ pdfinfo test_inkscape_wk0.pdf | grep 'Page size' Page size: 595 x 842 pts (A4) ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48317456/115864763-9da62500-a437-11eb-8761-0a72cf00e83a.png) ----- Here is the PDF produced by `wkhtmltopdf` with arguments to set page size - page size in itself seems correct, but the visuals are not: wkhtmltopdf.exe --page-width 1000pt --page-height 200pt test_inkscape.svg test_inkscape_wk1.pdf * [test_inkscape_wk1.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6364939/test_inkscape_wk1.pdf) ``` $ pdfinfo test_inkscape_wk1.pdf | grep 'Page size' Page size: 1000 x 200 pts ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48317456/115865185-46548480-a438-11eb-8a29-e905caec0e0b.png) ----- Here is the PDF produced by `wkhtmltopdf` with arguments to set page size and margins - page size in itself seems correct, but the visuals are not (extra margins still are present): wkhtmltopdf.exe -L 0in -R 0in -T 0in -B 0in --page-width 1000pt --page-height 200pt test_inkscape.svg test_inkscape_wk2.pdf * [test_inkscape_wk2.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/6364942/test_inkscape_wk2.pdf) ``` $ pdfinfo test_inkscape_wk2.pdf | grep 'Page size' Page size: 1000 x 200 pts ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48317456/115865243-5e2c0880-a438-11eb-8c62-789b6eeb0a3d.png) **Expected behavior** It should be possible to explicitly set a PDF page size for standalone SVG (or for an "empty" HTML file which simply "includes" the SVG graphic), and have the SVG drawn correctly inside the PDF (without extra margins). (EDIT: also on https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67212836/wkhtmltopdf-export-svg-file-to-pdf-tight-without-margins)

Run a successful wkhtmltopdf, but redirect STDOUT & STDERR to separate files.
```bash
wkhtmltopdf <parameters> 1>out.txt 2>err.txt
```

Note that `out.txt` will be empty, and `err.txt` will have all messages.

**Expected behavior**
Expectation would be that only errors are written to STDERR, and progress/success messages are written to STDOUT.

**Possible Solution**  
Pipe messages to the appropriate output stream.

title: Manage HTTP request delay
body: **wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: wkhtmltopdf 0.12.5 (with patched qt) **OS information** Linux Mint 20 **Description** When rendering several pages that contain some images, if images' source is a path (``), `wkhtmltopdf` will no render all HTTP-downloaded components . The result is non-determinist: sometimes some images are on the PDF, sometimes none (very rarely all of them are rendered). I think `wkhtmltopdf` does not like delays... I made some local tests with a HTTP server that adds some random delay on the requests, here is the result: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UudWfWWnYf6P2DiA50eRcHMofUqhSrcS/view?usp=sharing As you can see, when using a fast HTTP server, all is ok. But when adding some delays, the result is random... `wkhtmltopdf` seems to request all components (CSS and PNG files) but does not render all of them (see the second page, the QR code is missing) and it is not possible to predict which components will be correctly rendered -> I think this comes from the random delay... Sometimes `wkhtmltopdf` even renders only the first page. **How to reproduce** See video above. You need an http server open on port 8069. And, here are the files: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1w7YUSlqX1zLt24xyOZJlBH7rs6TJE2q0/view?usp=sharing Here is the CL used: `/usr/local/bin/wkhtmltopdf --disable-local-file-access --log-level error --page-size A4 --margin-top 0.0 --dpi 90 --zoom 1.0666666666666667 --margin-left 0.0 --margin-bottom 0.0 --margin-right 0.0 --orientation Portrait /tmp/src/reportb0.html /tmp/src/reportb1.html /tmp/OUTPUT.pdf` **Expected behavior** See the beginning of the video. While the HTTP requests are correctly processed, the rendering must be correct too. **Possible Solution** Add an option to manage the delay/time-out of the HTTP requests and make sure that `wkhtmltopdf` correctly renders the downloaded components.

Using wkhtmltopdf via a library in python called [pdfkit](https://pypi.org/project/pdfkit/) I am having issues rendering a simple HTML file with **only** references to css and NO javascript via a **reverse proxy (SSL enabled)** nginx server. We get an error describing HTTP 403 forbidden access to routes/urls that are never references in the HTML.

```
  File "/home/bender/mb-resume/app/blueprints/main.py", line 166, in resume
    pdf = pdfkit.from_string(resume_html, False, options=options)

```python

```

**Possible Related Issues**

title: Prevent access to internal resources via iframe and object elements
body:
**Description**
When the HTML content is untrusted, an attacker can render internal pages using an iframe, effectively using wkhtmltopdf as a proxy. Originally discovered by @adamgold:

> For example, when rendering a pdf using an AWS instance, http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ could give an attacker access to private keys:
>
> ```
> <iframe src="http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"></iframe>
> <object data="http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/" width="400" height="300" type="text/html"></object>
> ```

**Possible solutions:**

* Add a new option `--disable-frames`
* Only allow access to a list of trusted domains/IPs
* Prevent access to a list of forbidden domains/IPs

Build wkhtmltopdf (preferably through ports)

$ make

**Expected behavior**
Succesful build

**Possible Solution**  
Two errors produced.

1)

In file included from /usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSCell.h:31,
                 from /usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSObject.h:31,
                 from /usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/wtf/DateMath.cpp:79:
/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSValueInlineMethods.h: In constructor 'JSC::JSValue::JSValue(JSC::JSCell*)':
/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSValueInlineMethods.h:233:57: error: cast from 'JSC::JSCell*' to 'int32_t' {aka 'int'} loses precision [-fpermissive]
         u.asBits.payload = reinterpret_cast<int32_t>(ptr);
                                                         ^
/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSValueInlineMethods.h: In constructor 'JSC::JSValue::JSValue(const JSC::JSCell*)':
/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSValueInlineMethods.h:249:78: error: cast from 'JSC::JSCell*' to 'int32_t' {aka 'int'} loses precision [-fpermissive]
         u.asBits.payload = reinterpret_cast<int32_t>(const_cast<JSCell*>(ptr));

2) 

/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSGlobalData.cpp: In static member function 'static void JSC::JSGlobalData::storeVPtrs()':
/usr/ports/converters/wkhtmltopdf/work/qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/wtf/Assertions.h:326:74: error: size of array 'dummysizeof_JSArray_must_be_less_than_storage' is negative
 #define COMPILE_ASSERT(exp, name) typedef int dummy##name [(exp) ? 1 : -1]
                                                                          ^
                                                                              ^
                

Fix for #1:

Line 233 and 249 (same fix) of qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSValueInlineMethods.h changed from:
        u.asBits.payload = reinterpret_cast<int32_2>(ptr);
to
        u.asBits.payload = reinterpret_cast<long>(ptr);


Fix for #2:

Line 326 of qt-5db36ec/src/3rdparty/webkit/Source/JavaScriptCore/wtf/Assertions.h changed from:
#define COMPILE_ASSERT(exp, name) typedef int dummy##name [(exp) ? 1 : -1]
to:
#define COMPILE_ASSERT(exp, name) typedef int dummy##name [(exp) ? 1 : 0]


WARNING! I am obviously not a C-programmer, and I take no responsibility of the implications of the above changes on other platforms, but on arm64 these simple changes makes it possible to produce a wkhtmltopdf binary that's working fine - for me! I am especially worried about my "fix" for #2, which probably should be solved in another way.

title: Horizontal display of the vertical photo taken with the phone.
PDF Layers
body:
**Description**

https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/pdf-layers.html

The PDF spec enables the use of layers which have adjustable visibilities in Adobe Acrobat Reader. I haven't seen this functionality enabled in wkhtmltopdf.  

The layers could be marked by a special keyword in HTML, so wkhtmltopdf knows which elements represent the different layers.

**Example**  

If you convert an HTML document that includes SVG drawings that use `<g>` tags for layers, you could want the layers to be enabled separately.

There are some CAD programs that have this functionality. ([example 1](https://www.cad-notes.com/how-to-add-autocad-layer-information-in-pdf-file/), [example 2](https://knowledge.autodesk.com/support/autocad/learn-explore/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/How-to-turn-off-layers-in-your-AutoCAD-PDF-Plots.html))

I also found the reference explaining how layers (OCGs) are stored in PDF documents: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34096142/how-are-layers-stored-in-pdf

title: Generate PDF with password - user / owner password
body:
**Description**
It would be so useful to be able to set a user password and/or owner password as part of generating a PDF - thus allowing the PDF to be more secured so it prompts for the password upon opening. Being able to set a password when its generated would be ideal and useful to many people who deal with more sensitive PDF contents containing personal data etc.   Helps to tick another GDPR box!

PDF Font (Permissions?) Issue with Windows / Apache / wkhtmltopdf
body:
I have run into what is (apparently) a permission issue when loading fonts while running wkhtmltopdf under Apache on windows.  I have a document that is being translated from English to other languages (in this example, Bengali but I've also seen this behavior translating into Chinese and languages that have significantly different symbol sets).  Using the attached sample files, when I run the following command line under Apache in response to a user's input, the document contains the portions of the text which are to remain in English but small black squares are placed instead of the text in Bengali (Translated_via_Apache.pdf).  However, if I run the same command line in a CMD (or powershell) window the document is generated appropriately and text from both languages appear (Translated_via_CMD.pdf).

OS: Windows 10
Apache: 2.4 (64-bit)
wkhtmltopdf: 0.12.6 (64-bit)

`wkhtmltopdf --margin-bottom 0.75in --page-width 8.5in --dpi 250 --no-outline --quiet --debug-javascript --page-height 11.0in --margin-right 0.5in --print-media-type --load-media-error-handling abort --margin-top 1.1in --disable-smart-shrinking --margin-left 0.5in --load-error-handling abort --enable-local-file-access --header-spacing -10 --header-html "file:///d:/TempPDF/Header.html" --footer-html "file:///d:/TempPDF/Footer.html" page "file:///d:/TempPDF/Document.html" "d:\TempPDF\Translated.pdf"`

The output created from running wkhtmltopdf under Apache is logged and the following is what I get when running the above command.  When I run this in a CMD window, no output is written to the window. 
> QFontEngine::loadEngine: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngineWin: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngine::loadEngine: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngineWin: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngine::loadEngine: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngineWin: GetTextMetrics failed ()
QFontEngine::loadEngine: GetTextMetrics failed ()
(repeated a dozen more times)...

I've done quite a bit of searching and have found a couple of similar sounding issues:
1) [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56992378/iis-output-results-qfontenginewin-failure-when-running-wkhtmltopdf-process-fro](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56992378/iis-output-results-qfontenginewin-failure-when-running-wkhtmltopdf-process-fro)
2) [https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/3506](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/3506)

I've tried rebooting but that does not resolve this issue.  I have one machine where this problem does not occur and the only difference that I have found is that Apache is running under Local System rather than a specific user account (required for my system to support access to attached storage).  Has anyone else run into permission issues running wkhtmltopdf, or issues with running wkhtmltopdf from Apache? परीक्षार्थियों के लिए मुख्य अनुदेशः
1. ई-प्रवेश पत्र प्रोविजनल है, परीक्षार्थी को परीक्षा में बैठने से पूर्व अपनी पात्रता के सम्बन्ध में संतुष्ट हो जाना चाहिए।
2. फोटो पहचान पत्र के आधार पर पहचान सुनिश्चित हो जाने एवं गहन तलाशी के उपरान्त ही परीक्षार्थी को केन्द्र में प्रवेश दिया जायेगा। फोटो पहचान पत्र हेतु निम्न दस्तावेज मान्य होंगे - मतदाता पहचान कार्ड, आधार कार्ड, पेनकार्ड, पासपोर्ट, ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस आदि। पहचान प्रमाण पत्र की छाया प्रति मान्य नहीं होगी।
3. परीक्षा के दिन परीक्षा केन्द्र पर केवल निम्न सामग्री लानी हैः-
  i.  ई-एडमिट कार्ड।
  ii. 2.5 cm x 2.5 cm  साइज का नवीनतम रंगीन फोटो (उपस्थिति पत्रक पर चिपकाकर लायेंगे)।
  iii. नीली स्याही का पारदर्शी बॉल पेन।
  iv. फोटो युक्त पहचान पत्र।
4. परीक्षा के दिन परीक्षा प्रारम्भ होने के लिए नियत समय से एक घन्टा पूर्व परीक्षा केन्द्र पर आवश्यक रूप से उपस्थित हो जावें ताकि सुरक्षा जांच एवं पहचान का कार्य समय पर पूर्ण हो सके। देरी से आने पर तलाशी में समय लगने के कारण परीक्षा में शामिल होने से वंचित हो सकते हैं, अतः समय पर उपस्थित होना सुनिश्चित करे।
5. ओ.एम.आर. शीट में अधूरे/गलत रोल नम्बर भरने वाले, दो या दो से अधिक अभ्यर्थियों द्वारा एक ही रोल नम्बर भरे जाने पर गलत रोल नम्बर भरने वाले अथवा गलत स्थान पर बैठने वाले अभ्यर्थियों को मूल्यांकन प्रक्रिया से पृथक किया जा सकेगा।
6. विभागीय वेबसाइट https://rpsc.rajasthan.gov.in पर ई-प्रवेश पत्र के साथ उपलब्ध निर्देशों का अच्छी तरह से अध्ययन कर उनकी पालना करना सुनिश्चित करें।
7. सर्दी के मौसम के मद्देनजर गर्म कपडे एवं शूज (shoes) पहनकर परीक्षा में बैठने हेतु अनुमत किया जाता है।
8. परीक्षा केन्द्रों पर अभ्यर्थियों की गहन सुरक्षा जांच (Frisking) की जाएगी अतः आपकी सुविधा के लिए अनुरोध है  कि परीक्षार्थी लाख/कांच की पतली चूड़ियों के अलावा अन्य कोई जेवरात पहनकर नहीं आयेंगी परीक्षार्थी परीक्षा केन्द्र में किसी भी प्रकार की घड़ी, मौजे, धूप का चश्मा, बैल्ट, हैण्ड बैग, हेयर पिन, गण्डा/ताबीज, कैप/हैट, स्कार्फ, स्टॉल, शौल, मफलर पहनकर परीक्षा में शामिल नहीं होंगे।
9. परीक्षा केन्द्र में किसी भी परीक्षार्थी को परीक्षा प्रारम्भ होने के 10 मिनट के पश्चात् प्रवेश नहीं दिया जायेगा।
10. परीक्षार्थी परीक्षा कक्ष में अपने लिए निर्धारित सीट पर ही बैठे, अन्य सीट पर बैठने पर उनकी अनुपस्थिति दर्ज की जा सकती है।
11. किसी परीक्षार्थी को ई-एडमिट कार्ड साथ लाए बिना परीक्षा में बैठने की अनुमति नहीं है।
12. परीक्षा समाप्त होने पर अभिजागर के ओ.एम.आर. उत्तर पत्रक एकत्रित करने के पश्चात् ही परीक्षार्थियों को अपनी सीट छोडने की अनुमति होगी।
13. परीक्षार्थी प्रश्न पत्र पर दिए निर्देशों का भलीभाति अध्ययन कर लें।
14. परीक्षा के दौरान परीक्षार्थी प्रश्न-पत्र बुकलेट का कोई भी पृष्ठ या उसका हिस्सा अलग नहीं करेंगे। ऐसा करने पर आयोग द्वारा आपराधिक प्रकरण दर्ज कराने के अलावा दण्डात्मक कार्यवाही भी की जा सकेगी।
15. परीक्षार्थी को परीक्षा सम्पन्न होने के पश्चात् प्रश्न-पत्र बुकलेट और ओ.एम.आर. उत्तर पत्रक की कार्बन प्रति साथ ले जाने की अनुमति है।
16. आयोग द्वारा आयोजित परीक्षाओं में विशेष योग्यजन अभ्यर्थियों को स्वयं का श्रुतलेखक (scribe) लाने हेतु अनुमत किया जाता है, ऐसे अभ्यर्थियों को एक वचन-पत्र (Under-taking) प्रस्तुत करना होगा, जिसका प्रारूप आयोग की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है। साथ ही ऐसे अभ्यर्थी जो स्वयं का श्रुतलेखक (Scribe) नहीं लाते हैं, वे परीक्षा की नियत तिथि से दो कार्य दिवस पूर्व केन्द्राधीक्षक को सक्षम चिकित्सा अधिकारी द्वारा जारी किये गये प्रमाण-पत्र के साथ इस सुविधा के लिए आवश्यक रूप से आवेदन प्रस्तुत करें अन्यथा सुविधा उपलब्ध कराना संभव नहीं होगा। अभ्यर्थी श्रुतलेखक के संबंध में विस्तृत अनुदेशों का आयोग की वेबसाइट पर अवलोकन करें।
17. यदि आयोग द्वारा गठित पैनल में से अभ्यर्थी श्रुतलेखक चुनना चाहता है तो, परीक्षा से दो दिवस पूर्व कलेक्टर कार्यालय में स्थापित कन्ट्रोल रूम पर अभ्यर्थी को उपस्थित होकर श्रुतलेखक नियुक्ति हेतु निवेदन करना होगा। इस संबंध में आयोग की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध विस्तृत निर्देशों का अवलोकन करें।
18. ओ.एम.आर. उत्तर पत्रक में निर्धारित प्रविष्टियों/उत्तर के गोले गहरे करने के अलावा कोई भी निशान या संकेत या लिखावट लिखना दण्डनीय है। कृपया उत्तर पत्रक ( ओ.एम.आर.) भरने से पूर्व उसके कार्बन प्रति पर दिये निर्देशों को ध्यान पूर्वक पढने के बाद ही ओ.एम.आर. शीट में प्रविष्टियां करें। ओ.एम.आर. शीट पर उत्तर में सही का निशान लगाना, आंशिक गोला भरना या गोले के अतिरिक्त पेन का छोटा या हल्का पाइन्ट भी लगाया जायेगा तो उस स्थिति में भी जवाब गलत माना जायेगा।
19. परीक्षा के दौरान किसी भी प्रकार के अनुचित साधन का प्रयोग करने पर परीक्षार्थी के विरूद्ध अनुचित साधनों के उपयोग की रोकथाम के प्रावधानों के अन्तर्गत कार्यवाही की जायेगी।
20. आयोग के निर्देशों का उल्लघंन करने पर परीक्षार्थी के विरूद्ध उसकी परीक्षा रद्द करने और भविष्य में आयोग की किसी भी परीक्षा में बैठने से रोकने की दण्डात्मक कार्यवाही की जा सकती है।

body:

Linux Mint 20

Trying to generate a PDF that includes CSS from bootstrap causes a _floating point exception_.

`Loading pages (1/6)

Including the following in a HTML page causes the issue:

`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://stackpath.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/4.4.1/css/bootstrap.min.css" integrity="sha384-Vkoo8x4CGsO3+Hhxv8T/Q5PaXtkKtu6ug5TOeNV6gBiFeWPGFN9MuhOf23Q9Ifjh" crossorigin="anonymous">`

Then running:
`wkhtmltopdf --enable-local-file-access /path/to/html.html /home/user/out.pdf`

or even trying to generate the PDF from the bootstrap page itself:
`wkhtmltopdf https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.4/getting-started/introduction/ /home/user/out.pdf`

**Expected behavior**
Should generate a PDF including bootstrap CSS and/or fonts.

/Parrent 8 0 R\

===
0.12.5

Ubuntu 18:04

Problem
===
Not rendering well:

How to reproduce
===
To reproduce a fresh install, just run a docker file with these contents:

    FROM ubuntu:18.04

        apt-get install -y ./wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb && \
        :
    
    CMD [ "bash" ]

This creates a fresh ubuntu 18.04 and installs wkhtmltopdf v 0.12.5 and essentially does nothing else.

Then from the inside, I do a simple image render:

    wkhtmltoimage https://www.coronamaze.org/ca/ /files/coronamaze.jpg

When using the same fonts embedded in CSS as base64-encoded data urls, the rendered text looks very different when generating the PDF on different operating systems.

**How to reproduce**
See BasicInvoice.html in the attached zip file.

[wkhtml_font_difference_oses_case.zip](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/4281852/wkhtml_font_difference_oses_case.zip)

`wkhtmltopdf BasicInvoice.html Wkhtml_0_12_5_BasicInvoiceUbuntu18.pdf`
- on Windows
`wkhtmltopdf BasicInvoice.html Wkhtml_0_12_5_BasicInvoiceWindows10.pdf`

Open the resulting PDF file with some PDF viewer. I tested with Chrome built-in PDF viewer and also with PDF-XChange Viewer.

What you should see:
- zeros (0) look weird in Ubuntu PDF - they have thickening on their tops
- the difference between bold and regular fonts is much more noticeable in Windows PDF
- letter placement is slightly different - Windows PDF has some row headers split into two rows, while Ubuntu PDF has them on single line

**Expected behavior**
When embedding fonts in CSS and using the same wkhtmltopdf version, I expect the resulting text to look the same on all operating systems.

Otherwise it gets difficult to develop HTML templates on Windows when on the server (Ubuntu) they look so different.

title: Please use CWD as base path for files provided over stdin
body:
Currently wkhtmltopdf defaults file path to /tmp if html file is piped into the program.
This is not expected behavior and requires html files either to use only absolute paths or to define base path in html.
Please change the behavior so that in case of stdin file base path is defaulted to current working directory. Or if this is not possible for some reason, add a command line parameter that lets user to define the base path.

This request is connected to #2393, which was closed with a workaround without actual resolution.

title: wkhtmltoimage: load-error-handling and load-media-error-handling not reflected in exit code.
body: **wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.5 **OS information** - `Ubuntu Bionic 18.0.4 LTS` (package installed manually from `https://downloads.wkhtmltopdf.org/0.12/0.12.5/wkhtmltox_0.12.5-1.bionic_amd64.deb`) - `4.19.79-1-MANJARO` (package installed from Arch Linux Community repository) **Description** When rendering a webpage or html document to an image, the error handling command line options are ignored. Specifically: ` --load-error-handling ignore --load-media-error-handling ignore `. EDIT: If the program is given an output path the image is generated, but if you let it run the generated image to stdout instead, no image is generated. This different behaviour is counterintuitive, and even when an image is generated, it is also a little strange to get an error exit code when the program did run succesfully. **How to reproduce** Save the following to `input.html`: ``` ``` The URL above returns 403 Forbidden, it is an invalid URL on purpose. :) Then run: ``` wkhtmltoimage --format png --load-error-handling ignore --load-media-error-handling ignore input.html image.png ``` This gives the following output: ``` Loading page (1/2) Error: Failed to load https://www.abbuildingproducts.co.uk/media/catalog/product/, with network status code 201 and http status code 403 - Error transferring https://www.abbuildingproducts.co.uk/media/catalog/product/ - server replied: Rendering (2/2) Done Exit with code 1 due to network error: ContentAccessDenied ``` An image is produced in `image.png`, but since the program exist abnormally, it not possible to detect this reliably. **Expected behavior** A file in `image.png` with the `` element missing., so a white image, depending on X/Qt settings. And maybe some log messages about the URL in the element being ignored/skipped but still a return-code of `0`. **Possible Solution** The options from `wkhtmltoimage --help` doesn't list the options specifically, but they do get accepted (invalid options usually result in an error and the help being printed). I can also see that the options are supported as "common" though: https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/blob/master/src/shared/commonarguments.cc#L213-L214 Wether they do anything or not I haven't checked, but they would be very useful to have working. If you need anything else, please let me know. :)

title: Error generating pdf in Windows Container.  Incorrectly trying to load content from network.
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.5

**OS information**
Windows 2019 Containers

**Description**
Trying to run DocFX so as to create pdf documentation as part of our build process inside a Windows Container.

When I shell into the container and run the .ps1 script that calls the DocFX command `docfx pdf` my documentation is created as expected.

When the .ps1 file is run automatically (i.e. via the `CMD` line of the Dockerfile) I receive the following error:

```
[19-08-21 03:17:45.440]Info:[PDF]Start generating PDF files...
Loading pages (1/6)
Error: Failed to load **http://xn--c-ndam4q/**build/tools/REDACTED/pdf/_raw/pdf/api/TOC.html, with network status code 3 and http status code 0 - **Host xn--c-ndam4q not found**
Error: Failed loading page http://xn--c-ndam4q/build/tools/REDACTED/TOC.html (sometimes it will work just to ignore this error with --load-error-handling ignore)
[19-08-21 03:17:49.985]
```

**How to reproduce**

1. Put a DocFx project (`docfx init -q`) in `\docfx_project`

2. Create a Dockerfile with :
```
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk:4.8

SHELL ["powershell", "-Command", "$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; $ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue';"]

RUN Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; \
    INVOKE-EXPRESSION ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://chocolatey.org/install.ps1')) ; \
    choco upgrade chocolatey ; \
    choco install docfx -y ; \
    choco install wkhtmltopdf -y ; \

COPY /docfx_project .
COPY build.ps1 .

CMD ["powershell", "build.ps1"]
```

3. Create `build.ps1`:
```
docfx metadata
docfx pdf 
```

4. Build and run the container (note the failure as mentioned above)
`docker build -t pdf_builder .`
`docker run pdf_builder`

5. Shell into the container and run command manually (note the operation is successful)
`docker run -it -v pdf_builder powershell.exe`
`.\build.ps1`

**Expected behavior**
Builds the pdf file as per usual.

**Possible Solution**  
I thought perhaps the user executing the commands is different under the two different scenarios but i've confirmed it is `User Manager\ContainerAdministrator` in both scenarios by inserting `Write-Host $([System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name)` into the `build.ps1` script and examining the output when run interactively and when not.

title: Inadequate ToUnicode CMap generation when using a font which has multiple Unicode codepoints asignment on a single glyph
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.5

**OS information**
Windows 10 Pro (1903)

**Description**
Some Japanese fonts has glyphs associated with multiple codepoints. For example, in "Meiryo" which is one of the standard font of Windows Japanese edition, and is popularly used as css font-family, glyph ID 2473 is associated with two codepoints, "日" (U+65E5) and "⽇" (U+2F47).
 The former one is basic daily-use Chinese character which means "day" or "sun", and the latter one is code for "radical", i.e. part or component of Chinese character, and rarely used. Number of "Chinese character and its radical" pairs looking identical like above example is around 150. Another standard font, "Yu Gothc" and "Y Mincho" also has these pairs. (I'm not sure but perhaps in Traditional Chinese font "Microsoft JhengHei", the situation is same.)

Wkhtmltopdf seems to generate a ToUnicode table from "glyph" subset. When htmls which contains U+65E5 is converted to PDFs, generated ToUnicode tables contain U+2F47 as a codepoint for glyph 2473. Because U+2F47 is found earlier than U+65E5 while finding the glyphID-to-Unicode reverseMap. These PDFs has no problem about viewing by human, but serious text garbling occur and it prevents searching and copy-and-pasting.

(This problem is not aware of when the PDF file is viewed with PDF.js on Chrome or Firefox, because PDF.js normalize "radicals" into normal Chinese characters. Please check it by Acrobat Reader.)

**How to reproduce**
Sample input file (html): [test.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/3382859/test.txt)
Sample output file: [test.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/3383269/test.pdf)
Sample command line:
ren test.txt test.html
"c:\Program Files\wkhtmltopdf\bin\wkhtmltopdf.exe" test.html test.pdf

Open test.pdf with Acrobat Reader (not PDF.js), copy the second Chinese character. It should be U+65E5, but you get U+2F47.

(Above procedure need Japanese font "Meiryo", which is included in Japanese Supplemental fonts, Windows 10 optional feature. [link](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-10-missing-fonts) But needless to reproduce it, the problem is clear at QFontSubset::getReverseMap(), it assumes a single Unicode codepoints for a single glyph.)

**Expected behavior**
Ideally, glyphs derived from different codepoints should be distinguished by different glyph ID, and text in htmls should be recoverable in PDFs.

For above sample, first Chinese character should be U+2F47 and second one should be U+65E5, when text is extracted from PDF.

**Possible Solution**  
To support multiple codepoints for a single glyph, I think glyph subset should be recorded as a array of glyph-codepoints pair, and ToUnicode CMap should be generated from that array. But I don't know nothing about Qt, so I don't know it is possible or not.

If it is not possible, normalization of "radicals" into normal Chinese character, may mitigate the impact of the problem. Because use of "radicals" is very rare, and also this normalization is not critical for most people. As a matter of fact, "radicals" is normalized into normal Chinese character by NFKD of Unicode standard. "radicals" exist at between U+2E80 and U+2FFF, and normal Chinese character exist at higher. So, as a dirty hack, in QFontSubset::getReverseMap(), when first found codepoint is "radicals", and second higher codepoint is found, we can adopt higher one. But normalization means for us that it becomes more difficult to use "radicals" and normal Chinese character separately depending on the context, it is not desirable solution.

title: Synchronous xhr over ssl fails for self signed certificate i.e. invalid certificate.
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.3.2 (Issue also present in latest version 0.12.5)

**OS information**
<!-- Your OS specification -->
Windows Edition : Windows 7 Professional
System Type : 64-bit OS  

**Description**
<!-- A clear and concise description of the problem. -->
Synchronous xhr over ssl fails with NETWORK_ERR: XMLHttpRequest Exception 101 for self signed certificate i.e. invalid certificate.

**How to reproduce**
<!-- Html/css code and/or command line arguments needed to reproduce the problem. -->

We have run the given below code snippet in latest QT Browser's (3.8.5 version) console to debug the problem as wkhtmltopdf engine is based on QT Browser.  

/*
 * Use url to fetch js resource over https server.
 * 
 * If https server has self signed certificate(invalid certificate) then the xhr.send throws 
 * XMLHttpRequestException(NETWORK_ERR: XMLHttpRequest Exception 101: A network error occured in synchronous requests).
 * 
 * If we fetch any js resource from https sever with valid certificate then problem won't happen 
 * (example url: https://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js)
 */
 
var url = ''; // Replace this with valid url.
var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
// Here request needs to be synchronous i.e. async false to reproduce the problem.
xhr.open('GET', url, false);
xhr.send(null);


**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

Synchronous xhr over ssl should work properly for self signed certificates in wkhtmltopdf.

**Possible Solution**  
<!--- Optional: only if you have suggestions on a fix/reason for the bug -->

This same kind of problem was reported in phantomjs and i think it is now resolved in phantomjs. Given below is the issue link for reference 
https://github.com/ariya/phantomjs/issues/10985

title: Content and footer/header not sharing same cookie.
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.5

**Description**
I need to collect some data from content when building footer. More about this here:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/wkhtmltopdf-general/RrMol7-IPtA
When creating PDF from multiple documents I create cookie in html header, this cookie value is available in all footers & headers and can be changed any time.
If I create cookie in html content, this cookie value is available among other documents.

But headers and contents don't share same cookie. Cookie from header is not available in documents and cookie from content is not available in headers/footers.
Using same `cookie-jar` doesn't help.

Actually I don't have to use cookies. This is the only idea I have to resolve problem problem for above link.

title: Adding a cover makes the TOC disappear
body:
**wkhtmltopdf version(s) affected**: 0.12.4  and 0.12.6-dev

**OS information**
Ubuntu 18.04 / bionic

**Description**
I would like to add a cover page in front of the TOC. My TOC uses a custom stylesheet. If I add the cover before the toc, the toc fails to render. If I add it after the toc, the TOC renders, but the cover sheet is in the wrong place.  

**How to reproduce**
My laundry list of command line arguments: 

The following works (no cover, toc)

```
wkhtmltopdf --quiet --page-size Letter --title "Programming with Java" --enable-toc-back-links --margin-top 20mm --margin-bottom 20mm --margin-left 10mm --margin-right 10mm 
  --outline --dump-outline build/toc.xml toc --xsl-style-sheet toc-style.xsl --toc-header-text "Table of Contents" page - --header-right "[doctitle]" --header-font-size 8 --header-spacing 8 --footer-right "[subsection]  [page]"  --footer-font-size 8 --footer-spacing 8 build/test.pdf
```

The following does not work (cover created, toc is an empty page)

```
wkhtmltopdf --quiet --page-size Letter --title "Programming with Java" --enable-toc-back-links --margin-top 20mm --margin-bottom 20mm --margin-left 10mm --margin-right 10mm 
  --outline --dump-outline build/toc.xml cover build/pdf-cover.html toc --xsl-style-sheet toc-style.xsl --toc-header-text "Table of Contents" page - --header-right "[doctitle]" --header-font-size 8 --header-spacing 8 --footer-right "[subsection]  [page]"  --footer-font-size 8 --footer-spacing 8 build/test.pdf
```

The following also "works", but the cover page is on the wrong side of the toc: 

```
wkhtmltopdf --quiet --page-size Letter --title "Programming with Java" --enable-toc-back-links --margin-top 20mm --margin-bottom 20mm --margin-left 10mm --margin-right 10mm 
  --outline --dump-outline build/toc.xml toc --xsl-style-sheet toc-style.xsl --toc-header-text "Table of Contents" cover build/pdf-cover.html page - --header-right "[doctitle]" --header-font-size 8 --header-spacing 8 --footer-right "[subsection]  [page]"  --footer-font-size 8 --footer-spacing 8 build/test.pdf
```

Note: using `page` and reading content from stdin

**Expected behavior**

I expect the custom style sheet for the TOC to render correctly even when there is a cover page in front of it. ;)



**Possible Solution**  
<!--- Optional: only if you have suggestions on a fix/reason for the bug -->

**Description**
Using version 11 rc1 creates dramatically smaller PDF files than any version 12 or higher when creating a PDF that uses large images in the HTML that should be resized by using --image-dpi.  My best guess is that versions 12 and up are not actually resizing the image based on the request from the --image-dpi parameter, but packing them all into the PDF without actually scaling them down.

**How to reproduce**
Regardless of the value supplies with the --image-dpi parameter the resulting PDF is the same time.

**Expected behavior**
Using smaller values for --image-dpi should result in smaller PDF sizes.

**Possible Solution**  
If this is indeed a failure to properly scale the images upon importing them to the PDF then that would need to be fixed.

title: wkhtmltopdf encode URLs which resulted in Chinese Wikipedia URL invalid
body:
Brifely, it seemed that wkhtmltopdf encode the URL aother time which make Wikipedia couldn't recognize the encoded-twice URL encoded URLs.

Here is my steps:

1. use `wkhtmltopdf` to downlaod GitHub Page.
	- `wkhtmltopdf https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/GitHub github.pdf`
2. Open the PDF.
3. Click the `Git` hyper link, everythig is right.
4. Click the `版本控制` hyper link and Wikipedia returns `请求的页面标题包含无效字符：“%E7”` which means the `The requested page title contains invalid characters: "%E7"`.

And I dig out the reason:

- The true URL of `版本控制` is `https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/版本控制`
- The correct encoded URL of original webpage is `https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC%E6%8E%A7%E5%88%B6`
- The wkhtmltopdf converted PDF URL is `https://zh.wikipedia.org/%25E7%2589%2588%25E6%259C%25AC%25E6%258E%25A7%25E5%2588%25B6`

If you try to encode `%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC%E6%8E%A7%E5%88%B6`, it will be `%25E7%2589%2588%25E6%259C%25AC%25E6%258E%25A7%25E5%2588%25B6`

However, when the wkhtmltopdf converted PDF URL is clicked, wikipedia only decode once not twice, so that will recognize the *invalid characters "%E7"*

title: Reference to missing file in combination with --disable-local-file-access reports blocked access, even if file would be allowed if present
body:
Consider a broken reference to a file C:\Content\x.png present in the source HTML.

Normally when the app attempts to load this reference, you get the "missing media" behavior:

```
Warning: Failed to load file:///C:/Content/x.png (ignore)
```

However, if you combine it with `--disable-local-file-access` and `--allow C:\Content` you get:

```
Warning: Blocked access to file
```

There are two problems with this:

1. The real issue is that the reference is broken - it would be allowed if the file were present!
1. There is no filename printed at the end of this message, so it is not possible to know which reference is broken even if you know that this error can occur due to broken reference.

For comparison, if an existing file is blocked, it is named:

```
Warning: Blocked access to file C:/Content/y.png
```

Used v0.12.4 on Windows.

title: --load-error-handling abort is not raising Error
body:
Using wkhtmltopdf 0.12.4 (with pathched qt), using --load-error-handling abort has no affect on HTTP error status codes such as 404 or 500.

E.g.
wkhtmltopdf.exe --load-error-handling abort http://getstatuscode.com/404 output.pdf
or
wkhtmltopdf.exe --load-error-handling abort http://getstatuscode.com/500 output.pdf

both generate the pdf successfully, and don't "abort" the conversion. Is this expected? I was expecting the conversion to fail and no pdf to be output. It does exit with: "Exit with code 1 due to  notwork error: ContentNotFoundError", but no error event is raised.

If you provide an invalid domain such as http://www.sdfsadfsdfdfs.com then the expected error event is raised with "Error: failed loading page http://www.sdfsadfsdfdfs.com (sometimes it will work just to ignore this error with --load-error-handling ignore)" and the pdf is not created. And, further more, if you specify "ignore" instead of "abort" in this situation, it works as advertised and creates the pdf without raising the error event. Does anyone know why this behaviour is not present with the HTTP error codes?

Are there any workarounds for this issue? I'm trying to get the error event raised if there are any HTTP load failures, so that we don't end up generating a pdf that could have missing parts. We're using a .Net wrapper (TuesPechkin) that hooks into these error events. The only solution I can see so far is to modify the wrapper so that it doesn't only rely on the error events to signify an error.

Thanks

title: Certain Microsoft Font Glyphs treated as "Hidden" by Acrobat
body:
Hello,
    I have a peculiar issue with PDFs generated using this program.  I'm running Arch Linux with the latest updates installed as well as the `ttf-ms-win10` fonts package ([more info](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Microsoft_fonts)) which seems to work great for allowing use/display of Microsoft Fonts for most things.  The wkhtmltopdf version I'm using is:

```text
community/wkhtmltopdf 0.12.4-1 [installed]
    Command line tools to render HTML into PDF and various image formats
```

And the version of Adobe Acrobat I'm using is `Adobe Acrobat XI Pro 11.0.14.16`

I have a workflow which involves converting HTML to PDF, and then using Adobe Acrobat (on windows) to work on the PDFs.  A new step which I've been trying to integrate is using the "Remove Hidden Information" tool (`Tools > Protection > Remove Hidden Information`) to remove metadata and hidden text within the PDF file.  This is where my issue lies.  

When using this tool on a PDF which contains certain Microsoft Fonts (as produced with wkhtmltopdf on my Arch System as detailed above), Acrobat for whatever reason identifies certain characters (Predominantly vertical characters like `i, I, l, 1`) as "hidden text" and will subsequently remove them.

This is what the PDF looks like from `wkhtmltopdf`:
![no_missing_letters](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2519449/30752385-22eb8af4-9f8a-11e7-934c-09bcf44feed6.png)

And after "Remove Hidden Information" from `Acrobat` is run:
![missing_letters](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2519449/30752386-22ec2f0e-9f8a-11e7-9f70-1a7244bce3b5.png)
As you can see, it becomes unusable.  (In this particular example, it seems to affect only the lowercase letter `l` (elle), however in other examples it will affect the other letters listed above)

I've tried tracking down this issue but have gone in loops for a large amount of time across various adobe forums, as well as issues for this project, to no avail.  

I've attached a sample HTML file (`test.html`) and the PDF resulting from using `wkhtmltopdf` (`test.pdf`) which, when opened in Acrobat and having the `Remove Hidden Information` tool run on it, produces the last PDF file (`test_acro.pdf`), which is illegible and unusable.

I've uninstalled the MS fonts, letting `wkthmltopdf` fall back to my regular (non-Microsoft) `DejaVu` fonts, and the issue disappears.  I'm unsure of how to proceed since everything except this particular scenario has worked well in the past, but going forward I'd like to be able to figure out why these particular characters are being treated as `Hidden Text` by adobe acrobat.

Running `pdffonts` on the first pdf (output by wkhtmltopdf) reveals: 

```
name                                 type              encoding         emb sub uni object ID
------------------------------------ ----------------- ---------------- --- --- --- ---------
Tahoma                               CID TrueType      Identity-H       yes no  yes      7  0
Calibri                              CID TrueType      Identity-H       yes no  yes      8  0
```

And after running the `Remove Hidden Information` tool in Acrobat:

```
name                                 type              encoding         emb sub uni object ID
------------------------------------ ----------------- ---------------- --- --- --- ---------
Tahoma-Bold                          CID TrueType      Identity-H       yes no  yes     20  0
Tahoma                               CID TrueType      Identity-H       yes no  yes     23  0
Calibri                              CID TrueType      Identity-H       yes no  yes     26  0
```

Seeing that the fonts are listed as "embedded" via `pdffonts`, I've tried to "unembed" them (or "fixing" the pdf) in various ways (using `gs`, `qpdf`, `mutool`, `pdftocairo`, `pdftk`) but to no avail. Looking at the "PDF Optimizer" dialog for the PDF output by wkhtmltopdf shows no embedded fonts:
![unembed_fonts_missing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2519449/30752456-5670b610-9f8a-11e7-9f82-4690da60efff.png)

And acrobat show the following for both the `test.pdf` and `test_acro.pdf`:
![adobe_fonts_wkhtmltopdf](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2519449/30752520-8774d82c-9f8a-11e7-9b29-5dbea47c015a.png)

Which is strange since it seems to consider the fonts subset while `pdffonts` doesn't.

I'm pretty stumped at this point.  If anyone would like any additional information in relation to this issue, please let me know.  
Thank you,
Chris

[test.html.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/1325019/test.html.txt)
[test_acro.pdf](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/1325016/test_acro.pdf)

title: Different margins for the cover page
body:
Hi wkhtml team!

First of all, thank you for the great product! I don't know how can I thank you enough - this product is really great! Thanks again - you're doing the great job.

My question actually has been asked multiple times at different forums but unfortunately there were no answer for that. And I think it is not possible within the current wkhtml API - probably you guys can advice if there is an ability to at least patch/build the custom version. We really need that..

The thing is that we don't want margin-top and margin-bottom to be applied to the COVER page. title: Improper line breaks before math when converting HTML with Mathjax
body:
I'm trying to convert a Markdown file to HTML and then to PDF using `pandoc` and `wkhtmltopdf`. I believe something is going wrong with interplay between `wkhtmltopdf` and the `--mathjax` option for `pandoc`. `wkhtmltopdf` is inserting a hard line break before inline math equations in the PDF. I think it's a bug with `wkhtmltopdf` because the HTML seems fine (to me). - wkhtmltopdf 0.12.3 (with patched qt) - pandoc 1.19.2 Compiled with pandoc-types 1.17.0.4, texmath 0.9, skylighting 0.1.1.2 - CentOS Linux release 7.3.1611 (Core) Here is a minimal example that demonstrates the issue: ```bash $ cat tmp.md This is the equation for a line $y = mx + b$. $ pandoc --from=markdown --to=html5 -c pandoc.css --mathjax --output=tmp.html tmp.md $ cat tmp.html

This is the equation for a line \(y = mx + b\).

$ ``` (I use `-c pandoc.css` to write the proper `` header.) This is how the HTML renders. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5393995/29467794-966ba180-83f6-11e7-8cc0-fa6e9b03ce4d.png) Then I run: ```bash $ wkhtmltopdf --javascript-delay 2000 tmp.html tmp.pdf ``` This is how the PDF renders. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5393995/29467757-74f7b9ee-83f6-11e7-92b8-4f3ced4d5552.png) A temporary workaround is to use `--katex` with `pandoc`. This fixes the spurious line break issue, but the baseline for subscripts are then incorrect. I believe this is a separate, additional issue. This looks right, using `--katex`: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5393995/29468117-c46193f0-83f7-11e7-904b-1b63fe8c4951.png) But this is not correct: ```bash $ cat tmp.md This is the equation for a line $y_i = mx_i + b$ with a subscript. ``` ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5393995/29468159-ef98c0f2-83f7-11e7-9923-0ac3e8ca2c62.png)

title: feature request: anti-widow option to eliminate page breaks
body:
It's often useful to print a webpage on exactly 1 page.  The problem is `wkhtmltopdf` needlessly forces users to choose an absolute boundary for page breaks (a4, a5, etc).

**The workaround**:  I use a `for` loop to cycle through all the page sizes, running `wkhtmltopdf` for each one of them, then run `pdfinfo` on every PDF produced to find the files with only 1 page.  The side-effect with this brute-force workaround is that some whitespace still appears.

**What's needed**: users need to be able to specify *aspect ratio* only, and no page breaks.  Then `wkhtmltopdf` should choose the smallest custom height and width that respects the aspect ratio and gets everything on one page.  The user can then print the PDF using their preferred paper size and the "shrink to fit" option.

This feature should be trivial implement, because if I understand correctly, `wkhtmltopdf` already renders the webpage as a single page internally, as an initial step.  It just needs to skip the page breaking.

title: Forcing multiple columns using --user-style-sheet has no effect
body:
This webpage is very narrow (a common problem) and thus results in a huge rightside margin of wasted space:

  https://www.klm.com/travel/de_en/prepare_for_travel/checkin_options/internet_checkin/index.htm

In principle, `wkhtmltopdf` should be able to create a 2 column document so that the whole A4 page can be used.  According to this workaround: https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/1872 it should be possible.  The method demonstrated in that workaround was to directly modify the original document (inconvenient).  Users should be able to use the `--user-style-sheet` option to force multiple columns, but it does not work.  E.g., this script demonstrates:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

fn_css=$(mktemp --suffix=.css)
fn_result=$(mktemp --suffix=.pdf)

printf '%s\n' 'body { height: 28em; -webkit-columns: 0 0; width: 50%; -webkit-column-gap: 2em; -webkit-column-rule: 1px solid black !important;}' >"$fn_css"

wkhtmltopdf --cache-dir /tmp --page-size a4 --user-style-sheet file://"$fn_css"\
           'https://www.klm.com/travel/de_en/prepare_for_travel/checkin_options/internet_checkin/index.htm' "$fn_result"
```

It's clear that `--user-style-sheet` is being used, but it's failing to create multiple columns.

(btw, the code formatting above is screwed up for some reason.  There are no backtics in the code, but github seems to lose track of them.)

title: Add Javascript output prefix
body:
Currently all JavaScript outputs are sent over `Warning` callback signal with the following format: `<file>:<line> <message>`. It would be nice if JavaScript messages could be distinguished from other warning messages sent. There are two solutions in my opinion: 

 - Add a prefix to the message: e.g. `js@<file>:<line> <message>` this way JavaScript messages can be easily filtered out.
 - Add a new callback especially for JavaScript messages and send all JavaScript related stuff over this callback instead of the `Warning` callback.

While the second option requires more work I think it makes the whole system clearer. The fact that all JavaScript messages are sent over the `Warning` callback instead of `Info`-`Warning`-`Error` (respecting the JavaScript message types) is confusing, makes no sense and never mentioned (related #3178).

title: --window-status not available for HTML header/footer
body:
As we have complexes javascript inside our header and footer, the correct solution would be to use --window-status to wait for the correct rendering.
Unfortunately, [e02ff7e](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/commit/e02ff7efaf7b617986fc11c08a693e203c64a465) broke this feature.

It would make more sense that --window-status is used for all HTML file (it just need to be clearly documented that the status should also be set in header and footer). Another possibility would be an option to enable or not --window-status for header/footer.

Unfortunately, I cannot test it, as I'm unable to compile it under VS2015.

title: Wrong Kerning (?) When Using Underline
body:
wkhtmltopdf 0.12.3 (with patched qt) Running on Mac OS X 10.11.6 Here is what I experience with some documents. I have a sequence that looks like this: `Text1 with a space Text2` In some instances, the space at the end of the first tab does seem to disappear, and the first text seems to not be separated from the second text at all. When I modify the text in the first group by e.g. adding or removing characters, or replacing characters, the space between the two characters (last non-space character in Text1 and first character in Text2) seems to change. In most cases, it does not even seem to produce the problem. This sequence however will show the problem: ```

F Ta aaaddd deeee eeeeg hikln noop rrrs stu vv abcdefgh ijklmn abcdef abcdef abcdef.

``` When I insert a line break into the HTML after the space at the end of the text in the first tag, the problem does not show up: ```

F Ta aaaddd deeee eeeeg hikln noop rrrs stu vv abcdefgh ijklmn abcdef abcdef abcdef.

``` When I load the document into Acrobat and place the cursor just in front of the first underlined character, I can use the left-arrow key and verify that there is a space recorded in the PDF, but it does not show up. That's why I thought it might be a kerning issue. Opening the HTML in Safari or Chrome does show the space before the underlined text correctly. Test files can be downloaded from here: http://khkonsulting.com/files/wkhtmlissue_20161207.zip The ZIP file contains a source file that has three p tags, the first one shows the problem, the second on is exactly the same code, but with a line-break inserted into the HTML, and the third one is a copy of the first one, but with some characters removed from the first element. I've added a PDF and JPG output file, created by just calling wkhtmltopdf or wkhtmltoimage without any arguments besides the input and output file name. There is also a screenshot of what it looks like when I open the document in Acrobat.

title: Lang attribute is ingored
body:
Hi All, I'm using wkhtmltopdf 0.12.4 (with patched qt) and trying to render a document that contains _Traditional Chinese_, _Simplified Chinese_, _Japanese_ and _Korean_. ```
Ja: 与 才 骨
Hant:与 才 骨
Hans: 与 才 骨
Ko: 与 才 骨
Emoji: 💩
``` Opening this document with Chrome I can see that each div is rendered using a different set of fonts. This is right since the same codepoints are rendered in different ways according to the language (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_unification) ![screen shot 2016-12-02 at 6 07 48 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2744094/20843124/68956a28-b8ba-11e6-982e-1566b556febd.png) The same HTML rendered with **wkhtmltopdf** do not give the same result (neither on Linux nor on Mac OSX). As you can see the same font is used to render all the divs which means that the lang tag is totally ignored (and the Emoji is totally messed up) ![screen shot 2016-12-02 at 6 12 21 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2744094/20843268/f3a8754c-b8ba-11e6-8061-aad2ad7113f6.png) Is there any way to address this issue?

title: rebaselining/upstreaming of patches present in Qt fork

milestone.title: 0.13.x
milestone.description: Issues fixed in the next major release

body:
This is a tracker bug, which lists changes which need to be ported/applied to the latest Qt. Ideally, all of them should be upstreamed for qtbase + qtsvg. For qtwebkit, we can either try to upstream it to qt (which is unlikely to accept API changes) or to the revived fork.

# qtbase

### Build-system
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@ac73828 detect patched Qt (only for qtbase)
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@9c10077 run headless on Linux

### PDF enhancements
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@baf0626
    * [x] support for external hyperlinks (merged in qt/qtbase@e9eeb68 and qt/qtwebkit@62dd2ad)
    * [ ] support for anchors/internal links ([Webkit bug](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=112081), fixed in [r208347](https://trac.webkit.org/changeset/208347) and [r208398](https://trac.webkit.org/changeset/208398))
    * [ ] support for generating PDF outlines ([QTBUG-3893](https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-3893))
* [x] wkhtmltopdf/qt@172ef0d fix PDF creation date (merged in qt/qtbase@b5c273c)
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@7658278 support for PDF forms
    * [ ] basic AcroForms support
    * [ ] add TextField support
    * [ ] add CheckBox support
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt#7 additional controls in PDF forms
    * [ ] add RadioButton support
    * [ ] add ComboBox support
    * [ ] add HiddenField support
    * [ ] add PageJavaScript support
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@6f3def4 allow printing of PDF form elements
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@c6e2d6b regenerate field appearances

### Image printing improvements
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@33a8e10 original monolithic patch
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@eced0bb added ARGB32_Premultiplied format support
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt#28 use smart-growing buffer for compression

# qtsvg
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@27dfb29
    * [ ] optionally clip objects that are outside the viewBox
    * [ ] do not output unused/duplicate state objects in QSvgPrintEngine

# qtwebkit

### Build-system
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@ac73828 detect patched Qt (only for qtwebkit)
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@9c10077 run headless on Linux
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@9c65bf9 build static WebKit
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@8dae19a allow override of screen resolution
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@fe194f9 fix -webkit-debug not being respected


### new APIs
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@f4915e5 webpage print control API
    - see comments in [Webkit 26584](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=26584)
    - split up into multiple patches, if possible
    - investigate using QPagedPaintDevice
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@874b2a3 using "screen" media-type
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@5509dcd custom print shrinking (used to disable)

### bugs
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@0306e5c incorrect page height computation
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@2cbc764 pass page height to printContext

### rendering improvements
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@b7c2c15 implement "page-break-inside: avoid"
* [ ] wkhtmltopdf/qt@53226bf improve font kerning
* [ ] table printing improvements
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@3e94723 prevent page breaks in table rows
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@b4ae708 table page-break improvements
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@71d412b ensure first cell when checking required table height
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@e4c9c73 handle edge-case with exactly fitting last table row
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@3ef69db fix segfault if table body does not have a cell at 0,0
    - wkhtmltopdf/qt@d2e9dda suppress blank page if first cell spans multiple pages

* [ ] DPI-related

title: Font sizes smaller than they should be
body:
Hi. I'm converting a web page that uses `font-family: Calibri`. In the resulting PDF the text appears smaller than expected. If I open the document in Acrobat, highlight a portion of the text and make change to the font, for example change its size or make it italic, and then reverse that change, the amended text is displayed larger than the unamended text, even though the font size and all other attributes are reported as identical by the Format panel.

If I save this and open it in the Windows program PDF-XChange Viewer, the original (too small) text is reported to be `CalibriRegular (Embedded)` and the modified larger (correct) size text is `Calibri (Embedded Subset)`.

Can anyone offer any insight into what's going on here?

title: Thin white margin always displayed on one side
body:
I just encountered the same bug discussed [here](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/1982), [here](https://github.com/mileszs/wicked_pdf/issues/223#issuecomment-243826272), and [possibly here](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/issues/2817).

It seems there is a thin white margin that is always present on the right side of portrait PDF, and on the bottom side of landscape ones, even though all margins are set to 0 both in the CSS and as wkhtmltopdf arguments.

The only fix that would work for me was to specify `--page-height 297mm --page-width 212mm` in addition to 0 margins, like so:

```
wkhtmltopdf --margin-top 0 --margin-bottom 0 --margin-left 0 --margin-right 0 --page-height 297mm --page-width 212mm test.html test.pdf
```

Since it seems to affect anyone wanting to have a full-width background other than white, I think it's a pretty major issue.

Any ideas ?
