title: [0.13] Ported qt hacks to qt 5.7

milestone.title: 0.13.x
milestone.description: Issues fixed in the next major release

body:
Mostly directed towards @ashkulz:

I have a functioning build on windows with most of the patches previously applied to qt 4.8.

Headless support and avoidance of page breaks in tables are not currently ported.

See the following repositories:
- https://github.com/poizan42/wkhtmltopdf
- https://github.com/poizan42/qtbase
- https://github.com/poizan42/qtwebkit-5-wk
- https://github.com/poizan42/qtsvg-5-wk

This also contains the work I did in wkhtmltopdf/qt#10 but split into smaller commits. Feel free to cherry-pick. Note that the build script in wkhtmltopdf currently has nsis package generation disabled and generates visual studio projects and may not work on non-windows platforms. I'm intending to make it a bit more flexible so you can use it to generate what you want from the commandline.

The following patches are currently not ported:
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@8dae19a82231e87366d81c683bafcb025aea9c1d: allow override of screen resolution using environment variables
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@a5393b1f3301743c01808cd8e9aa663739309a19: change screen size to a more sane value (1366x768)
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@409e09ad48968a787d332d8a1c5944bc8a8f275a: make table page-break logic opt-in via CSS at the row level
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@d2e9dda38d1e80ac4aba01f09053388c35115b33: suppress blank page generated if the first cell spans multiple pages
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@3ef69dbb856f99c4dae1e9d548ad3a7cc551dedd: Fix segfault when checking heights for pagination if table body does not have a cell at 0,0
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@e4c9c7389821d32c3ec94cc818ce0f47af9b394b: Handle page break edge case with exactly fitting last table row
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@71d412b0652f2bf8500f8c2b2428bc79247d5c93: Ensure we have a first cell to measure when checking required table height
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@b4ae70897e8a1b0debaa85af982e27c253f4d337: Table page-break improvements
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@2cbc7640b7be5988d28e236a2624c59bac59c858: Pass page height through to print context from web frame printer
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@2179f6a95257fbaed1deb40da0eeb3ee86bd2b9f: Repeat thead and tfoot when table contains page breaks.
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@3e947239fa3b8d96738e44fe5d551f9b67bfcf63: Prevent page breaks in table rows.
- wkhtmltopdf/qt@9c1007780ba5e77f78cd6988cd115fdacc2866c3: Remove some graphics dependencies

The page break in tables handling should be done when calculating layout and not in the rendering. Some of it may already have been fixed upstream. Other additions should probably be added to the new "upstream" home for QtWebKit at https://github.com/annulen/webkit.

Also I'm planning on updating wkhtmltopdf to use the new QtWebKit instead once they have their first stable release.

title: Too many open files issue
body:
Hello team, recently we ran into an issue in which converting a big html to pdf succeed but part of the images missing.

OS: Ubuntu 1204
wkhtmltopdf 0.12.3 (with patched qt)
After a further investigating with strace, we found that wkhtmltopdf is trying to open image files and never close the file descriptor until reaching the max number of file descriptor. 

``` bash
ulimit -n
1024
```

and here is part of the strace output: 

```
stat("/etc/localtime", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=388, ...}) = 0
stat("/imagepath1", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=83753, ...}) = 0
open("/imagepath1", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 1023
fcntl(1023, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC)        = 0
fstat(1023, {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=83753, ...}) = 0
stat("/etc/localtime", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=388, ...}) = 0
stat("imagepath2", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=155306, ...}) = 0
open("imagepath2", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 EMFILE (Too many open files)
lstat("imagepath3", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=155306, ...}) = 0
stat("imagepath3", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=134171, ...}) = 0

```

`imagepath1`, `imagepath2`, `imagepath3` are general image files, and you would see `too many open files` error when the file descriptor id reached 1024.

as a result we keet seening errors like `Warning: Failed to load file:path to image file` in the terminal.

we sometimes do have more than 1024 imagew in a single html doc, Increasing limitation by set ulimit should be temp a solution, but can we make some changes to wkhtmltopdf itself?

title: --page-offset when combining multiple documents is incorrect
body:
So a project I'm building is outputting some 8 documents (some with/without cover pages) and we'd like to also produce an "omnibus". I did the logical from reading the documentation...

```
cover cover-a.html body-a.html cover-b.html --page-offset=-27 body-b.html
```

This was just the experiment but pages are now numbered from -26..27. So I figured maybe I need to specify the offset for the first document...

```
cover cover-a.html --page-offset 0 body-a.html cover-b.html --page-offset -27 body-b.html
```

To no effect. Still numbered from -26..27.

Looks like there's no way (currently) to convert multiple documents into one with their original numbering. Especially when you factor in that those documents I used were dynamic and could easily shrink/grow, and I wouldn't know what to set that offset to.

If it isn't too hard, could we have an option to completely reset page numbering (current and total) as if the document had ended? I know mine isn't the typical use-case, but I'm certain that someone else out there would like it.

EG: --reset-page-numbers would completely reset the current and total number of pages before handling the current page/cover.

title: wkhtmltopdf does not work using --javascript-delay or --window-status in conjunction with plotly.js
body:
Hi, I'm not sure if this is an issue with wkhtmltopdf or plot.ly or both, but wkhtmltopdf does not work when using a plot.ly graph. Part of the problem, unsurprisingly, is the need to wait for the rendering to complete. However, even when using --javascript-delay, wkhtmltopdf does not seem to be able to run the plot.ly javascript properly.

Furthermore, if using --window-status, then no code after the plotly call is run, suggesting that the javascript execution encounters some kind of error and stops. 

For example, using the attached ex.html and ex2.html (you will have to change their extensions back from txt to html), both of work fine in Chrome:
`wkhtmltopdf --window-status this_does_not_execute_with_wkhtmltopdf_but_it_should ex.html test.pdf`
will hang forever

But if you look at ex_with_alert.html in a browser, you can see that the code that sets this_does_not_execute_with_wkhtmltopdf_but_it_should

Perhaps the wkhtmltopdf javascript engine is not able to execute the plot.ly javascript?

[ex_with_alert.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/64278/ex_with_alert.txt)
[ex.txt](https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/files/64277/ex.txt)

title: Absolute Positioning does not push siblings down with Page-Break-Inside rules
body:
I have a pdf that is laid out with absolute positions and there are some long divs that span multiple pages. They have repeating headers for the thead element so that the resulting div when printed is actually quite a bit taller than calculated in the HTML. 
The next sibling starts where the previous left off, however, since the previous was stretched down it should also stretch down. It does not! See attached photo for an example.
Note on the bottom right is the position that was calculated based on height and then where it says "real:" I get the offset of the DIV to the right of it, so this is a real "top" offset. 
Then notice on the left of the page I have a ruler for keeping track of the absolute positioning values of the page. Note how the bottom should end at 5407 but it really ends at 5700px, therefore, the next sibling should start at 5700, not 5482. 
If there is a way to fix this please let me know.

title: Documentation request: --javascript-delay versus --window-status, who wins?
body:
In [the documentation](http://wkhtmltopdf.org/usage/wkhtmltopdf.txt), it says:

```
  --javascript-delay <msec>       Wait some milliseconds for javascript
                                  finish (default 200)
```

and:

```
  --window-status <windowStatus>  Wait until window.status is equal to this
                                  string before rendering page
```

But if you specify both, who wins?

I found [a forum posting](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/wkhtmltopdf-general/vWDe5hUAyJ8) which says:

> "--javascript-delay 100000 --window-status myrandomstring" 
> This will cause wkhtmltopdf to output the pdf as the document looks 
> after 100 seconds, or when window.status is set to myrandomstring 
> whatever comes first. 

That sounds great, but empirically, it is not what wkhtmltopdf 0.12.2.1 does here.
- If I specify `--window-status` only, it waits a couple seconds until my JS code sets window.status to that value.
- If I specify `--javascript-delay` to 100000, it waits around 100 seconds (or a little more).
- If I specify both, it waits for the longer time.

Either way (max or min), it would be great if the documentation told me what I should expect here.

thanks!

title: page-break-inside behavior
body:
64-bit MinGW wkhtmltopdf 0.12.2.4 with patches on Windows 7 SP1

I have some very long tables in the HTML, and need to split them across multiple pages. If I use CSS:

```
td { page-break-inside: avoid; }
```

it seems to ignore this (fails to avoid breaking) _AND_ the `<thead>` overlaps the first line or two of the row content (e.g., the "y" coordinate of the thead and the content are the same). If instead I use

```
tr { page-break-inside: avoid; }
```

it _does_ avoid splitting a row, and starts the next row (with a thead) on the next page. However, two minor problems:
1. The left and right borders are drawn all the way down to the bottom of the page, even though there is no content.
2. If the row is the first of the table, it gives the thead and the left and right borders on this page, and then repeats the thead on the next page and renders the row.

Using the "tr" method, it's just a cosmetic issue, but I'd like to do it cleanly (and properly, if I'm doing it wrong or there's a better way).

title: Segmentation fault while rendering a SVG using fill pattern based on SVG image
body:
I am trying to render a page which embeds a SVG using a referenced SVG image in a fill pattern, like in this simplified example:

``` html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
    <svg xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="300" height="200" version="1.1">
        <defs>
            <pattern id="pattern" x="0" y="0" width="10" height="10" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
                <image xlink:href="/test-pattern.svg" x="0" y="0" width="5" height="5"></image>
            </pattern>
        </defs>
        <g>
            <rect fill="url(#pattern)" x="0" y="0" width="300" height="200" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1"></rect>
        </g>
    </svg>
</body>
</html>
```

and the test-pattern.svg:

``` xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" width="5" height="5">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="5" height="5" fill="#005599"></rect>
</svg>
```

Running `wkhtmltopdf 0.12.3-dev-79ff51e (with patched qt)` 64bit on OS X, I get a segmentation fault:

``` sh
% /usr/local/bin/wkhtmltopdf 'http://localhost/test.html' test.pdf
Loading pages (1/6)
Counting pages (2/6)
Resolving links (4/6)
Loading headers and footers (5/6)
Printing pages (6/6)
Segmentation fault===========================================] Page 1 of 1
```

There are no problems rendering the SVG in Safari or Chrome. 

When embedding the `test-pattern.svg` code directly within the `<pattern>` tag instead of using `<image xlink:href=... >` there is also no problem.

I've noticed when I omit the xmlns declaration `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` in `test-pattern.svg` or changing it to `foo`, no seg fault occurs, but the rectangle will be rendered empty. Don't know if this is somehow relevant.

title: Running out of system timers
body:
I have a very large input document consisting of around 3000+ pages. I've tried to convert source html to pdf, while applying header and footer as another html file.

After a while of running this tool, I get the error message:
**QEventDispatcherWin32::registerTimer: Failed to create a timer (The current process has used all of its system allowance of handles for Window Manager objects.)**

For the sake of illustration, these are the numbers currently allocated items:
LEAK: 19565 SubresourceLoader
LEAK: 19596 CachedResource
LEAK: 19588 Frame
LEAK: 705329 RenderObject
LEAK: 790180 WebCoreNode
LEAK: 19588 Page

This issue is reproducible using very large input document - I have tested it on a empty html file, containing 600k line breaks. Additional headers and footers were empty, but were added using --header-text-html and --footer-text-html.

I believe that this issue is partially caused by javascript delay in multipageloader.cc:

`if (!ok || signalPrint || settings.jsdelay == 0) loadDone();`
`else if (!settings.windowStatus.isEmpty()) waitWindowStatus();`
`else QTimer::singleShot(settings.jsdelay, this, SLOT(loadDone()));`

I have tried to turn jsdelay to 0, but without any success.

title: page-break-before and page-break-after rules ignored within floating parent elements
body:
The easiest way to describe is with an example: https://gist.github.com/mtalcott/67df9917438308f55eaa

The two HTML files, test_breaks1.html and test_breaks2.html, are only different in that the outer div in test_breaks2.html has a `float: left` rule. While test_breaks1 renders as three separate pages, as desired, 
test_breaks2 renders as a single page and ignores the page-break CSS rules.

I've seen some other issues with page break rules not working as expected, but nothing with clear examples of what's going wrong. I suspect that a lot of people coming across this behavior might find this info helpful.

As a workaround, we're using PDF-specific CSS to apply `float: none` rules on parent elements that we need page breaks within.

title: [0.13] Css media issue? `print` vs `screen` ?
body:
To reproduce : https://github.com/laguiz/wkhtmltopdf-issue-css
# wkhtmltopdf 0.13 issue with css ?
## My Config
- wkhtmltopdf 0.13.0-alpha-7b36694
- Windows 7 Pro SP1
## Description

I use Bootstrap to format my CSS. In `0.12` all is ok but in `0.13` css seems loaded with media `print` so we have differences between HTML and PDF with `0.12` and `0.13`. I mainly discovered that **backgrounds** are not display properly but we may have bigger impact.
## Questions
- Is it expected to have a difference with media usage between `0.12` and `0.13`?
- If `print` is the normal behaviour then background are not displayed as expected but then how we can display background out of the box? Any trick?
## How to reproduce the issue ?
- You need node installed (or any http serveur)
- `git clone git@github.com:laguiz/wkhtmltopdf-issue-css.git`
- `cd wkhtmltopdf-issue-css`
- (with node) `http-server` in root folder
- Go to http://127.0.0.1:8080/ and make sure you see Bootstrap components properly (with backgrounds and proper fonts)
- Open new console and try to reproduce doing : `wkhtmltopdf.exe http://127.0.0.1:8080/ resultko.pdf`
- In HTML change `style media` to `all`, `print`, `screen` and see differences.
## My observations
- I had to set `all` or `print` for media styles to make sure we see something close to what we see on `screen`.
- With media `screen` it's like css are not loaded (maybe expected feature if `print` is the media selected)
- With wkhtmltopdf 0.12 everything works with media `screen` so we don't have differences between screen and our pdf.

Feel free to ask.

We've been running into a problem recently, some pages don't seem to work when the `--height` option is omitted (or manually set to 0)

```
D:\Tools>wkhtmltoimage.exe -V
wkhtmltoimage 0.12.2.1 (with patched qt)
```

Without the `--height` option:

```
D:\Tools>wkhtmltoimage.exe http://www.reanmachine.com/this-is-a-test/ d:\out.png
Loading page (1/2)
Rendering (2/2)
Error: Will not output an empty image
QPainter::begin: Paint device returned engine == 0, type: 3
QPainter::translate: Painter not active
QPainter::setRenderHint: Painter must be active to set rendering hints
QPainter::setBrush: Painter not active
QPainter::pen: Painter not active
QPainter::setPen: Painter not active
QPainter::end: Painter not active, aborted
Error: Could not save image
Done
Exit with code 1, due to unknown error.
```

With the `--height` option:

```
D:\Tools>wkhtmltoimage.exe --height 1000 http://www.reanmachine.com/this-is-a-test/ d:\out.png
Loading page (1/2)
Rendering (2/2)
Done
```

This is problematic since we don't know the target height, it should be inferring it from the rendered content.

This occurs on Windows 8.1, Windows 2008 R2, and Windows 2012

title: wkhtmltox fails to delete temp files when wkhtml_deinit is called right after wkhtmltopdf_destroy_converter
body:
\- and probably leaks memory too.

`wkhtmltopdf_destory_converter` uses `deleteLater()` on `converter`. `PdfConverter::~PdfConverter()` also uses `deleteLater()` on its `PdfConverterPrivate` instance. Apparently destroying the application afterwards does not ensure that the enqueued deletes are processed.

Changing all those `deleteLater()` into regular deletes makes the problem go away. Do we actually need to use `deleteLater()` for those cases? Can we ensure that the resources are properly freed before destroying the application some other way?

title: unreachable IMG src path, with invalid ext on URL gets ContentNotFoundError
body:
If I have an -img src- in my HTML, and if the src property does not end with a valid extension, I got ContentNotFoundError.

If I put ".png", it passes just saying the resource was not found. (this is ok, resource is not supposed to be find).

Its is a problem if my original HTML makes reference to a system that generates images on the fly, and does not have any extension, because it will be resolved on the browser by mime-type. I believe wkhtmltopdf is trying to do the same, and fails because could not understand what type this image would be, and does not worry that the target is indeed unreachable. Happens with http, file and direct path access.

I believe if wkhtmltopdf can try to reach the URL BEFORE trying to checking for 200, it would abort normally saying the resource cannot be located. If it CAN be located, well, all will then go fine...

The only workaround I have here is to check exit code, and if it is not zero, call wkhtmltopdf again, with --no-images, and look for exit(0).

I understood that your exit(1) means pdf generated with some trouble, but usually exit(1) mean errors. So I cant monitor if exit(1) is this situation, or something else.

title: acroreader renders ugly fonts when a page has a transparency
body:
Original ticket from google code: https://code.google.com/p/wkhtmltopdf/issues/detail?id=99

This is still a problem in 0.12 (tested on Fedora 19, built from master), looks to be a "feature" where acroreader defaults Transparency rendering to the CMYK colour space [1][2].

This text needs to be added to the page object in the PDF on any page with a transparency:

/Group << /S /Transparency /I true /CS /DeviceRGB>>

I tested this by building a  PDF and manually adding the above text to the first page (it has an SVG logo with transparency) then acroreader stopped making it ugly.

$ wkhtmltopdf -V
Name:
  wkhtmltopdf 0.12.1-development
...
  Compiled against wkhtmltopdf patched qt.

PDF diff:

 5 0 obj
 <<
 /Type /Page
 /Parent 2 0 R
 /Contents 64 0 R
 /Resources 66 0 R
 /Annots 67 0 R
 /MediaBox [0 0 595 842]
+/Group << /S /Transparency /I true /CS /DeviceRGB>>

> >  endobj

I was tempted to submit a patch hard coding this in QPdfEnginePrivate::writePage ... but I'm not sure if any other colour space should be exposed for transparency.

1: http://tug.org/pipermail/pdftex/2007-December/007480.html
2: http://forums.adobe.com/thread/714292

title: overlapping text when repeating headers/footers in table

milestone.title: future
milestone.description: planned for sometime in the future

body:
When having a big table with lots of rows, or many tables with 10-20 rows, sometimes the feature that repeats the thead/tfoot when there is a page break causes weird results.

Like a tfoot is moved to page one, and is displayed above some other text.

Can this feature be turned off?
